account: A 75-year-old man surnamed Chen, with controlled hypertension, woke one day with chest tightness and palpitations that were first taken for reflux. Liberty Times puts the onset in 2021. At China Medical University Hospital in Taichung, his exercise electrocardiogram was read manually and scored with the Duke Treadmill Score. That reading put him at moderate risk with about 50 percent narrowing and called for follow-up only. The hospital's own Exercise ECG AI-Assisted Interpretation System, in use since May 2022, put the probability of severe narrowing (over 70 percent) at 72 percent. Cardiologist 吳宏彬 then ordered angiography. It found a 99 percent stenosis of the left anterior descending artery, which he stented at once. He said that the manual reading would have led to drug treatment and follow-up only. He put the man's chance of an acute infarction at 8 in 10. The man went home, and his chest tightness resolved. The hospital presented the case on 28 December 2022. Test and procedure dates are not reported. The three news reports of 28 December 2022 carry the hospital doctors' account and quote no one outside the hospital.

ai_role.statement: The model read the exercise-ECG signals and report features. It returned a 72% probability of severe coronary narrowing, above the moderate-risk verdict of the manual reading and risk score. On that basis the cardiologist ordered angiography, which showed the 99% stenosis, and he stented it. The counterfactual rests on the treating cardiologist's statement, carried by three outlets and the hospital's release. He said the manual reading would have led to drug treatment and follow-up only. The hospital that says so also built the model. The dates of the reading and procedure are not reported. The published model's specificity of 0.60 means such flags are often false positives.

fields.account: A 75-year-old man surnamed Chen, with controlled hypertension, woke one day with chest tightness and palpitations that were first taken for reflux. Liberty Times puts the onset in 2021. At China Medical University Hospital in Taichung, his exercise electrocardiogram was read manually and scored with the Duke Treadmill Score. That reading put him at moderate risk with about 50 percent narrowing and called for follow-up only. The hospital's own Exercise ECG AI-Assisted Interpretation System, in use since May 2022, put the probability of severe narrowing (over 70 percent) at 72 percent. Cardiologist 吳宏彬 then ordered angiography. It found a 99 percent stenosis of the left anterior descending artery, which he stented at once. He said that the manual reading would have led to drug treatment and follow-up only. He put the man's chance of an acute infarction at 8 in 10. The man went home, and his chest tightness resolved. The hospital presented the case on 28 December 2022. Test and procedure dates are not reported. The three news reports of 28 December 2022 carry the hospital doctors' account and quote no one outside the hospital.

purpose: The hospital's AI Center built the system to judge from an exercise electrocardiogram whether a patient's coronary arteries are severely narrowed (over 70%). The hospital says that manual reading of a dozen tracings is slow and only 40–50% accurate. Flagging this patient's severe stenosis falls within that purpose.

ratings.reason: A man with a 99 percent stenosis of the left anterior descending artery had it stented after the software flagged a 72 percent probability of severe narrowing. The manual reading of his exercise electrocardiogram had rated his risk moderate and would have left him to drug treatment and follow-up. The cardiologist put his chance of an acute infarction at 8 in 10. He said that the stent removed the risk of sudden death. The man left hospital, and his symptoms resolved. The hospital's headlines call the case life-saving. The harm was prospective, and the only account comes from the hospital that built the model, so a life saved is not established.
